incident: Conti ransomware against the Irish Health Service Executive (HSE)

sources.title: Conti cyber attack on the HSE - Independent Post Incident Review (PwC, via HSE)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (spearphishing Excel to Patient Zero workstation), hop (to an HSE server / IT systems of 1 statutory + 6 voluntary hospitals), impact (encryption + data exfiltration)

sources.title: Conti PWC Attack Flow (CTID attack-flow corpus)
sources.what_it_gave: machine/edge structure: patient-zero workstation -> HSE server -> hospital IT systems

narrative_before: On 18 March 2021 a user at the HSE (Patient Zero) opened a malicious Microsoft Excel attachment delivered by spearphishing, compromising the workstation (PwC report). The actor then compromised high-privilege accounts and an HSE server, and moved laterally into the IT systems of one statutory and six voluntary hospitals. Over the following weeks the actor browsed and exfiltrated data and, on 14 May 2021, detonated Conti ransomware across the environment, encrypting systems and forcing the HSE to shut down its national IT infrastructure. The attack disrupted health services nationwide for weeks.

detection_moments.description: Initial access: Patient Zero workstation compromised by opening the malicious Excel attachment.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Malicious Microsoft Excel file is attached to a phishing email ... User ... clicks on malicious Excel file, compromising the workstation.' - Conti PWC flow / HSE PwC report

detection_moments.description: HSE server compromised via high-privilege account abuse and lateral movement into hospital IT systems, before mass encryption on 14 May 2021.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Compromise and abuse accounts with high privilege levels ... Lateral movement to 1 statutory and 6 voluntary hospitals' - Conti PWC flow / HSE PwC report

attack_path: privileged account abuse to reach HSE server - T1586 / T1078
lateral movement into statutory/voluntary hospital IT systems - lateral movement (technique not sub-typed in report)
ambiguities: Report/flow does not name individual hosts beyond 'Patient Zero workstation' and 'HSE server'; the 1 statutory + 6 voluntary hospital systems are modelled as a generic group capped at 3 machines.
Exact lateral-movement technique between HSE server and hospital systems not sub-typed in the flow; left generic.
Detection moment: the flow gives no defender-detection timestamp; m2 marks the pre-encryption lateral stage (first public knowledge ~14 May 2021).
